content:
mara: Heads up — Kibana returns partial matches when I try to join logs by trace_id across eu-west1 GPU nodes, queries keep timing out. Anyone else?

dmitri: saw a couple of grafana alerts around loki query latency for eu-west1 earlier. Which query are you running?

mara: simplest repro: in Kibana Logs with KQL I do `trace_id: "bb3a8f..."` then union with pod logs, but the Dashboard trace join panel times out. Using time range ~1m around the event.

mara: pasted raw Loki query I used in Grafana:
```
{cluster="eu-west1", job="gpu-logs"} |= "bb3a8f" | json | line_format "%{trace_id} %{msg}"
```

aline: alert-bot fired earlier: `ALERT loki_query_latency_p95 (eu-west1) > 12s` — I muted a noisy rule but this looks real.

alert-bot: alert: loki_query_latency_p95 firing for cluster=eu-west1 (started 3m ago) :fire:

jonas: any chance this is caused by cross-region shard hop? we recently backfilled indices and changed retention on central longterm store.

dmitri: can you share `loki_query_duration_seconds_bucket` for the period? also `ingester_memory_bytes` for the loki pods. high ingress + large regex or `|=` with many labels can blow up.

mara: metrics pasted into channel: `loki_query_duration_seconds_bucket{le="10"}=0.2, {le="30"}=0.78, {le="60"}=0.98` — p95 ~ 45s.

infra-sre: repro steps I suggest: 1) run the exact LogQL in a grafana Explore for eu-west1 with `limit=1000` and `timeout=30s`; 2) if it times out, try same query with `|~ "trace_id=bb3a8f"` for a lighter match; 3) run `kubectl -n loki logs` on ingesters to check tailing backpressure.

mara: tried reducing time range and adding `|= "trace_id"` first — still slow for that cluster.

dmitri: quick check: are we normalizing trace IDs? we had a mix of v0/v1 formats and occasional truncation during upstream proxy. If some logs store truncated ids, join becomes wide.

aline: I see `gpu_pod_evictions_total` spike around same timeframe on prometheus. maybe eviction churn causing many restarts and mangled logs across shards.

jonas: patch suggestion: increase loki `query_range.timeout` for eu-west1 from 20s -> 60s for the short term and add a p95 alert at 30s, and then tune `table_manager` retention compaction to reduce index size.

mara: agree. also adding a normalized `request_id` at ingress would make joins far cheaper than searching by arbitrary trace snippets.

dmitri: I'll open a quick PR to increase timeout and update alert threshold. infra-sre — can you run `kubectl get pods -n loki -o wide` and check ready counts?

infra-sre: running now, one loki-ingester-2 shows `CrashLoopBackOff` and high OOM in events. I'll redeploy with smaller local retention and cordon that node for GPU provisioning until evictions settle.

deploy-bot: redeploy started: loki/ingester -> image:v2.3.1 (initiated by infra-sre).

mara: after redeploy I can reproduce but p95 is down to ~7s. Good for now. Thanks all — follow-ups: normalize ids at ingress, increase timeout, and add query_rate limiter per user to prevent heavy full-text scans.

dmitri: created PR #412 to bump eu-west1 loki query timeout + alert change, will link the runbook.

aline: I'll add a one-liner in the SLO dashboard notes about query latency variance during eviction windows.

jonas: recorded action items: (1) PR #412, (2) ingress trace normalization ticket, (3) temporary timeout bump, (4) follow-up compaction plan. Closing thread once PR merged. :white_check_mark:
